intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: TOTEM measures protons and particles from LHC collisions, so it is idle while the LHC is shut down; this is an inference, since no TOTEM-specific statement about this shutdown was found. Status is shutdown, not upgrade. No source consulted says that TOTEM's own detector is being modified in LS3. Start and end are the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 3 dates. CERN's 5 August 2026 item says 'The cryogenics team has been running the warm-up sequence since LS3 began on 29 June 2026' and that the stored helium is kept 'ready to be used again once the accelerator resumes operation in mid-2030'; CERN's 29 June 2026 article says 'The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030'. The end is a schedule value, not a reported event.
intervals.quote: Following its final physics run, the accelerator has been switched off to begin CERN’s Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) ... The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030

name: TOTEM
notes: kind is recorded as 'collider' (an LHC forward-physics measurement experiment sharing IP5 with CMS, not a standalone accelerator/fixed-target/neutrino/etc. experiment); no more specific enum value fits a diffractive/elastic cross-section experiment at a collider IP, so 'collider' plus the topic_ids/physics_goals context is used to distinguish it from CMS itself.
As of 2026-10-25 the official TOTEM site (totem.web.cern.ch) redirects to a CERN single-sign-on login page and could not be read; home.cern and the INSPIRE experiment record were used instead.

Run/shutdown intervals from Run 1 onward are the LHC-wide machine schedule (accelerator:lhc and the other LHC experiments' records) applied to TOTEM, since no TOTEM-specific run-by-run announcement was found; the 2015 CMS-TOTEM combined-measurement partnership is the one TOTEM-specific fact confirmed independently.
No results or technical documents are recorded for TOTEM yet.

physics_goals.quote: The total cross section will be measured using the luminosity independent method which based on the simultaneous detection of elastic scattering at low momentum transfer and of the inelastic interactions. This method also provides an absolute calibration of the machine luminosity.
physics_goals.value: Measure the total, elastic and diffractive proton-proton cross sections at the LHC, and provide a luminosity-independent absolute calibration of the machine luminosity

summary.plain: TOTEM sits around CMS's collision point and measures protons that barely miss each other, letting physicists work out the total chance that two protons collide at all -- one of the most basic numbers in particle physics.
summary.technical: Forward-physics experiment sharing LHC interaction point 5 with CMS: 26 Roman Pot detectors plus T1/T2 forward tracking telescopes, ~3000 kg of equipment spread over ~0.5 km, measuring total, elastic and diffractive pp cross sections via the luminosity-independent method. Proposed August 1997, approved November 1999, first data November 2009; ran combined measurements with CMS from 2015.

unique_capabilities.quote: the Roman pot is moved toward the machine axis by compressing the bellows until the inner edge of the detectors reaches a distance of the order of one millimeter from the beam
unique_capabilities.value: Roman Pot detectors that move silicon sensors to within about 1 mm of the circulating beam once it is stable, detecting protons scattered at very small angles that no other LHC detector can reach
